requirements.requirement: Create a helpdesk account on node1 as an ordinary, non-administrative user.
requirements.summary: The account was initially absent, then created with its own UID, private group, home directory, and no administrative group memberships. Its account and home remained present after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Allow helpdesk to restart the SSH service through sudo.
requirements.summary: Direct tests from the helpdesk identity restarted sshd successfully. The service PID changed, and sshd recovered active, listening, syntactically valid, and serving an OpenSSH banner both before and after the node reboot.

requirements.requirement: Grant helpdesk no administrative privileges beyond restarting the SSH service.
requirements.summary: The effective sudo policy lists only the two equivalent exact sshd restart commands. Policy and execution checks denied arbitrary root identity execution, a root shell, service status, another service restart, and the permitted restart with an extra argument.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The supplemental node-restart protocol is also complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot identity were captured, the restart was acknowledged, the boot identity changed, and system, SSH, account, policy, and functional restart state recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the transition.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Account creation and sudoers installation directly implemented the task; the two bounded sshd restarts validated functionality and post-reboot recovery; and the scheduled reboot fulfilled the mandatory restart protocol. None required reversion. Final observations show no failed services, healthy package state, expected listeners only, and merely reboot-regenerated systemd private temporary paths.
